description:
We are Team Local Build from Thrissur! We are Civil Engineering students who love solving real local problems using NASA data and space tech.

We are working on land, farming & Earth observation ideas. We are looking for team members with skills in Coding, Data Visualization, Design & Storytelling. Join us to build something simple, useful & impactful!
summary: FieldWise Kerala is a bilingual web-based project that helps farmers explore crop rotation ideas using NASA Earth observation data and local farm information. It uses NASA POWER data to show temperature and rainfall conditions. Farmers can enter details such as soil type, water availability, and current crop to compare different crop rotation options. The project aims to support sustainable farming, improve soil health, and help farmers make better decisions. It is designed especially for Kerala farmers and supports both English and Malayalam.
details: Project Details – Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data FieldWise Kerala is a bilingual web-based prototype designed to help farmers explore suitable crop rotation ideas using NASA Earth observation data and local farm information. The website uses NASA POWER data to display temperature and rainfall information based on the farm's location. Farmers can enter details such as soil type, water availability, current crop, and farming priorities. Based on these inputs, the website provides illustrative crop rotation options to help farmers compare different possibilities. The main benefit of this project is that it helps farmers understand local weather conditions and explore different crop rotation strategies. It aims to support better farming decisions, encourage sustainable agriculture, improve soil health, and promote efficient water use. We developed the prototype using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. NASA POWER API is used to retrieve weather information, and GitHub Pages is used to host the website publicly. The creative aspect of our project is the combination of NASA Earth observation data with local farming information in one simple platform. It also supports both English and Malayalam, making it easier for farmers in Kerala to understand and use. While developing this project, we considered Kerala's local farming conditions, soil types, water availability, weather variations, farmers' priorities, and ease of use. The project is an educational prototype, and the suggested crop rotations should be confirmed with local agricultural experts before practical use.
